feeds.what: every state-level contest of the election in one document (173 ballot items: 3 state measures, 10 US House, 122 legislative, judicial, a few multi-county local), plus per-county election stubs, turnout statistics and voter registration
feeds.notes: Standard Enhanced Voting shape: …/results/public/api/elections/<slug>/<publicElectionId>/data. slug 'washington' (lower case), id '20261103'. 29,686 bytes gzipped on the wire. Cache-Control: public, max-age=60. The page says 'This page auto-refreshes and is updated in real-time'. The page also polls …/elections/washington/20261103/closeraces (returned '[]').

feeds.what: jurisdiction document with the elections list (4 elections in 2026) and the 39 counties
feeds.notes: NOTE the path: the elections list is at api/jurisdictions/<slug> (key 'elections': [{publicElectionId, electionDate, name, dateText}]). The older guess api/elections/<slug> answers 404 (saved as elections-list.json, 0 bytes).

election_id: '20261103' (publicElectionId = the election date as YYYYMMDD). Appears in the page URL /results/public/washington/elections/20261103 and the API URL /api/elections/washington/20261103/data. The internal GUID is election.id = 01000000-a578-3971-654b-08defdf81b1d.
discovery: GET https://results.votewa.gov/results/public/api/jurisdictions/washington and read .elections[] (publicElectionId, electionDate, name). Washington's ids have so far all been the date: 20261103, 20260804, 20260428, 20260210.
cors: none on 200 responses (no Access-Control-Allow-Origin, and the response carries 'cross-origin-resource-policy: same-origin'). Oddly a 404 from the same API does answer 'access-control-allow-origin: *'. A browser on openslate.us cannot read this directly; it needs the relay.
bot_blocking: Relay User-Agent: 200 for jurisdictions and data (behind Cloudflare, cf-cache-status DYNAMIC, no challenge). Browser User-Agent not needed. Headless Chrome also loaded the page fine. (Git Bash's curl 8.8.0/Schannel fails on this host with 'curl: (43)' during TLS renegotiation; Windows' own curl 8.22 works. That is a client bug, not blocking.)
updated_field: election.asOf = '2026-11-10T22:19:26.9976753Z' (UTC, ISO 8601 with 7 fractional digits) is what the page shows as 'Last Updated Tuesday, November 10, 2026 at 2:19:26 PM' (Pacific). Also election.lastUpdated = '2026-11-10T22:18:12.0964996Z', election.publishDate, election.publishVersionId (a GUID that changes with each publish). Each ballot item repeats it in reportingStatus.asOf.
reporting_field: Per contest: ballotItems[].reportingStatus.reportingUnits / .totalUnits, and in Washington the units are COUNTIES, not precincts (e.g. {"reportingUnits": 39, "totalUnits": 39} for a statewide measure, 2/2 for Congressional District 1; the page words it 'Counties reporting 39/39'). election.precinctsReporting is null and localityElections[].precinctsReporting is null: Washington (vote-by-mail) publishes no precinct progress. There is instead a statistics[] block 'Estimated Ballots Left to Count' by county.
choice_format: ballotItems[].summaryResults.ballotOptions[]: name is a language array [{"languageId":"en","text":"Suzan DelBene"}], voteCount 195433, party {abbreviation:"DEM", name:[{"languageId":"en","text":"(Prefers Democratic Party)"}]} (Washington's top-two 'prefers' wording, parentheses included; abbreviations seen REP, DEM, IND, LIB, NO, NON and oddities like DE2 '(Prefers Democrat Party)', LDP, NKP, CAC). Write-ins are a separate option 'Write-in' (or 'Write-In') with isWriteIn true and a null party. Nonpartisan judges have party.abbreviation null. Measures: contestType 'BallotMeasure', options named 'Yes' and 'No' with null party; the measure's explanatory text is HTML in ballotItems[].referendum. isWinner is null throughout.
district_field: Only in the title (name[0].text, e.g. 'Legislative District 6 - State Senator'). contestGroupId groups contests ('State Measures', 'U.S. Congressional Representative', 'Legislative', 'Judicial', and the literal 'other'); voteFor holds a loose label ('Legislative', 'Congressional', sometimes upper case), not a number. crossCounties lists the counties a multi-county contest spans.
terms: none found on the results page or in the API (footer links only to https://www.sos.wa.gov/elections/data-research/election-data-and-maps/election-results-and-voters-pamphlets). I did not search sos.wa.gov for a general terms page.
